title: Write scripts/ax-compile.py using DSPy MIPROv2 to generate v3 artifact
description: Create scripts/ax-compile.py using DSPy MIPROv2. (1) Load data/synthetic-jobs-v2.json as trainset — each example has inputs: leadName, leadTitle, company, angleType, topSignalType, topSignalDetail, whyNow; output: emailDraft (subject + body). Map from OutboundJob JSON fields (lead.name, lead.title, signals[0].type, signals[0].detail, etc.). (2) Define an outcome-aligned LLM judge metric function with two components directly mapping to business objectives: accept_score = 'Would an experienced SDR approve this draft without editing?' (0–1) and reply_score = 'Given this specific lead context and signal, how likely is this email to receive a positive reply?' (0–1). Composite: 0.4 * accept_score + 0.6 * reply_score (reply rate weighted higher as the ultimate signal). Critically: pass 2–3 gold examples from training data (positiveReply=true AND edited=false) as few-shot context in the judge prompt so the LLM is calibrated on actual labeled outcomes, not abstract quality intuitions. In --mock mode, replace LLM judge with a composite heuristic that directly mirrors the training labels: score = (0.4 if edited=False else 0.0) + (0.6 if positiveReply=True else 0.15) applied to training examples, then average. (3) Run MIPROv2 with num_candidates=5 and a GPT-4o teacher model. (4) Save optimized program instruction and top 6 demo examples to data/ax-optimized-v3.json: { instruction: string, demos: DspyDatasetRow[], compiledAt: string, optimizer: 'MIPROv2' }. Pre-commit the --mock output. Add requirements-dspy.txt with dspy-ai and openai.
acceptance_criteria: 1. scripts/ax-compile.py exists. 2. python scripts/ax-compile.py --mock runs without errors. 3. data/ax-optimized-v3.json has instruction, demos, compiledAt, optimizer. 4. Judge prompt explicitly references accept rate and reply rate as scoring axes. 5. requirements-dspy.txt exists.
notes: Model: GPT-5.4 xhigh. Metric is the key design decision — must be outcome-aligned (accept + reply rate), not structural. Few-shot calibration from gold labeled examples is critical.

title: Create data/prompt-snapshots.json with v1-v4 instruction artifacts
description: Author data/prompt-snapshots.json with entries for v1, v2, and v3. Schema per entry: version string, label (v1/v2/v3), releaseDate, instruction string, fewShotDemos count, summary, and (for v3) badgeText: 'MIPROv2 Optimized'. The v1–v2 instructions show realistic drift: v1 is a raw basic prompt; v2 adds angle-type guidance and sender/company context. The v3 entry is the MIPROv2-rewritten instruction — write a plausible, genuinely improved version: shorter, more precise, opens with the specific trigger signal, keeps under 80 words. Mark fewShotDemos: 6 for v3. The v3 entry will later be cross-checked against the Python MIPROv2 script output (bd-1nm), so write it in a way that looks like real LLM-in-the-loop instruction refinement.
acceptance_criteria: 1. data/prompt-snapshots.json exists with v1, v2, v3 entries. 2. Each entry has all required fields. 3. v3 instruction is noticeably and concretely better than v2. 4. Valid JSON.
notes: Model: Claude Sonnet 4.6 high. v3 instruction is the star — it should read like a real optimizer output: tighter, more signal-led, with specifics.

title: Generate 60-job synthetic corpus (30 v1 + 30 v2)
description: Create two JSON files: data/synthetic-jobs-v1.json and data/synthetic-jobs-v2.json, 30 jobs each. Each job must fully conform to the OutboundJob shape in lib/types.ts. Critical fields to populate for the DSPy pipeline: (1) signals: ScoredSignal[] — at least one signal per job with type (one of: trial_activation, hiring_signal, tech_migration, event_signal, web_intent, social_post), detail (1-2 sentence specific observation), body (URL or source detail), and score (0.6–0.95). (2) draft.subject and draft.body — realistic SDR email. Draft body should be 60–120 words, opening with a reference to the signal, closing with a CTA. (3) feedback.edited (boolean) and feedback.positiveReply (boolean) — positiveReply represents a rep marking a lead reply as positive in the review UI, emulated as it would be set in the real workflow. (4) status: 'sent_stub'. (5) promptVersions.draftGenerator: the correct version string. (6) lead.name, lead.title, company, whyNow, angleType, angle. Target ratios: v1 ~45% clean accept, 3-4 positiveReply=true; v2 ~65% clean accept, 8-10 positiveReply=true. Use varied companies, angle types, and signal types across both files. Do NOT write a generation script — author the JSON directly.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Two files in data/ with 30 jobs each. 2. Every job has a non-empty signals array with type + detail + body. 3. Every job has a draft.subject and draft.body. 4. feedback.positiveReply is set on all jobs. 5. Ratios are directionally correct. 6. Parses as valid OutboundJob[].
notes: Model: GPT-5.3-Codex xhigh. Do NOT write a script. Author JSON directly. The signals and draft fields are what MIPROv2 trains on — they must be realistic and varied.

title: Finalize label contract across feedback type, metrics, and export
description: Two changes: (1) Extend OutboundJob.feedback in lib/types.ts to include positiveReply?: boolean | null. Update computeDspyVersionMetrics in lib/metrics.ts to fall back to feedback.positiveReply when outcome is absent. Update scripts/export-dspy-dataset.ts to include the label. (2) Relabel the active queue jobs: in lib/mock-data.ts and scripts/seed.ts, change the active job promptVersions.draftGenerator from the current v3 string (2026-04-11.draft-generator.v3) to the v2 string (2026-02-17.draft-generator.v2). The demo narrative is: v1 and v2 are historical, v2 is the current live version the agent is running on, and DSPy optimization in the UI produces v3. This is a purely mechanical relabeling — no other logic changes.
acceptance_criteria: 1. feedback.positiveReply field exists. 2. metrics function works for synthetic jobs with no outcome. 3. Active jobs in mock-data.ts and seed.ts are stamped v2. 4. No TypeScript errors.
notes: Model: GPT-5.4 xhigh. Mechanical type + relabeling work.

title: DSPy tab demo interactions: Run Optimization, v4 reveal, Reset Demo
description: Add interactive demo behavior to DspyPage.tsx, plus a full workspace reset. (1) Run Optimization button: triggers a 4-5 second progress animation with a status log (e.g., 'Loading v2 corpus...', 'Running MIPROv2...', 'Scoring candidates...', 'Done.'). On completion, the v3 row unlocks in the version table and the prompt diff view switches to v2 vs v3 side-by-side. The button reads data/ax-optimized-v3.json (the precommitted artifact) — no live API call needed. (2) Reset Demo button (global, possibly in header/nav): calls POST /api/reset-demo, which re-seeds InstantDB by running the demo snapshot seed logic (see note below), then returns success. On success, the UI reloads to the initial snapshot state — queue cleared and repopulated with the curated job set, live agent state cleared, DSPy tab local state cleared (v3 hidden, diff reset, log cleared). (3) Demo snapshot definition: create data/demo-snapshot.json with a curated set of 10-15 jobs that tells a good pre-demo story: a mix of unreviewed, 1-2 approved, 1 archived, all stamped v2. This file is the source of truth for what Reset restores to. The /api/reset-demo route deletes all InstantDB jobs and re-inserts from this file. Model the route on scripts/seed.ts pattern.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Run Optimization button triggers animation and reveals v3. 2. Reset Demo button calls /api/reset-demo and restores queue. 3. data/demo-snapshot.json exists with 10-15 curated jobs. 4. /api/reset-demo route exists and re-seeds correctly. 5. DSPy tab state clears on reset. 6. No TypeScript errors.
notes: Model: Claude Sonnet 4.6 high for UI interactions and demo-snapshot.json curation. The /api/reset-demo route may need a brief architectural check with GPT-5.4 if InstantDB admin API requires special permissions.
